findings.evidence: lock a Member account after 5 consecutive failed login attempts within a 10-minute window
findings.rationale: Specifies the account lock trigger but omits the lockout duration, unlock/recovery procedure, and user error response.

findings.evidence: him
findings.rationale: The pronoun "him" has multiple plausible antecedents (the Librarian, the Member, or the Guarantor).

findings.evidence: TBD minutes
findings.rationale: Uses placeholder "TBD" instead of a concrete token expiration duration.

findings.evidence: user-friendly; easy to navigate; loads rapidly; standard connections
findings.rationale: Uses subjective, unquantified terms ("user-friendly", "easy", "rapidly", "standard") without measurable acceptance criteria.

findings.evidence: TBD consecutive times
findings.rationale: Uses placeholder "TBD" instead of specifying the maximum number of consecutive loan renewals.

findings.evidence: validate item eligibility within 2 seconds and issue the loan receipt
findings.rationale: Describes only the happy path after scanning a barcode without specifying system behavior or error handling when item eligibility validation fails.

findings.evidence: the allowed maximum number of active hold requests
findings.rationale: References a numeric hold limit without providing the actual maximum number.

findings.evidence: up to 8 physical items simultaneously
findings.rationale: Allows a Member to borrow up to 8 physical items simultaneously, conflicting with SD-009's limit of at most 5 physical items.

findings.evidence: 21 calendar days from the checkout timestamp
findings.rationale: Sets the standard loan period for circulating print books to 21 calendar days, conflicting with SD-010's 14 calendar days.

findings.evidence: Unverified visitors shall be able to self-register online with only an email address and immediately check out physical books without Librarian ID verification.
findings.rationale: Permits self-registration with only an email address and checkout without ID verification, contradicting SD-001's rule that a Librarian must verify government-issued photo ID and record full name, email, and phone number before account creation.

findings.evidence: remain held indefinitely until the requesting Member explicitly cancels the hold
findings.rationale: States reserved items remain held indefinitely until cancelled by the Member, contradicting SD-011's rule to cancel uncollected holds after 72 hours.

findings.evidence: and/or suspend borrowing privileges and/or apply a penalty flag
findings.rationale: Stacked "and/or" connectives make it ambiguous which combination of actions is mandatory or optional when an item is 7 days overdue.

findings.evidence: shall be reviewed, approved, and recorded
findings.rationale: Passive voice leaves unspecified which human role or system component is responsible for reviewing, approving, and recording fine waiver requests.

findings.evidence: if appropriate
findings.rationale: Uses the non-binding qualifier "if appropriate", making the dispatch condition subjective and untestable.

findings.evidence: TBD years
findings.rationale: Uses placeholder "TBD" instead of a concrete retention period in years.

findings.evidence: $1.25 USD per overdue day per item with no maximum cap on accumulated fines
findings.rationale: Specifies an overdue fine of $1.25 USD/day with no cap, conflicting with SD-019's $0.50 USD/day and $20.00 USD maximum cap.

findings.evidence: permitted to renew borrowed items online at any time regardless of any unpaid overdue fine balance
findings.rationale: Allows loan renewal regardless of unpaid fines, contradicting SD-020's rule blocking renewals when unpaid fines exceed $5.00 USD.

findings.evidence: Patron
findings.rationale: Introduces the term "Patron" instead of the established domain term "Member" used throughout earlier requirements (e.g., SD-001, SD-009).

findings.evidence: return search results quickly even when many users are querying
findings.rationale: Uses unquantified terms "quickly" and "many users" without a numeric latency threshold or concurrency target.

findings.evidence: where possible
findings.rationale: Uses the weak qualifier "where possible", making query term highlighting optional and unverifiable.

findings.evidence: sufficient ISBN matching accuracy and acceptable response times
findings.rationale: Uses subjective terms "sufficient" and "acceptable" without quantitative accuracy or response-time metrics.

findings.evidence: efficiently process large batch MARC21 files without noticeable system slowdown
findings.rationale: Uses vague terms "efficiently", "large", and "noticeable" without measurable throughput, file size, or performance degradation limits.

findings.evidence: shall detect the active references
findings.rationale: Specifies detecting active loans or holds on deletion attempts but omits the resulting system behavior (e.g., blocking deletion and returning an error).

findings.evidence: at TBD intervals
findings.rationale: Uses placeholder "TBD" instead of defining the database backup schedule interval.

findings.evidence: important administrative actions in a timely manner and retain them for an appropriate period
findings.rationale: Uses unquantified terms "important", "timely manner", and "appropriate period" without defining which actions, latency bounds, or retention duration.

findings.evidence: shall log event FAILOVER-01
findings.rationale: Only specifies logging an event when the primary database node is unreachable for more than 10 seconds, omitting the actual failover or recovery action.

findings.evidence: adequate transport security and clear error messages
findings.rationale: Uses subjective terms "adequate" and "clear" without specifying concrete protocols (e.g., TLS version) or error-message standards.

findings.evidence: accept any Member password of at least 8 characters
findings.rationale: Accepts any password of at least 8 characters, conflicting with SD-002's minimum of 12 characters and mandatory uppercase, lowercase, and numeric character classes.

findings.evidence: keep authenticated web portal sessions active for 60 minutes of user inactivity
findings.rationale: Sets the inactivity session timeout to 60 minutes, conflicting with SD-004's 15-minute inactivity timeout.

findings.evidence: encrypt all Member passwords using reversible AES-256 encryption so Administrators can decrypt and retrieve forgotten passwords
findings.rationale: Requires reversible AES-256 encryption so passwords can be decrypted, contradicting SD-003's requirement to hash passwords with bcrypt and never store plaintext.
